title: Chapter 5: Embeddings, Vector Databases, and Semantic Search
content:
Chapter 5: Embeddings, Vector Databases, and Semantic Search

When the wording changes

The RAG assistant in Chapter 4 loaded a PDF, split its text into chunks and used relevant passages to answer a question. Its keyword retriever worked best when the question and the document shared words. Consider this pair:

Question: What is the refund policy?

Document chunk: The refund policy allows customers to request a refund within 30 days.

The word “refund” gives the retriever a useful match. A reader might ask the same thing another way:

Can customers get their money back?

The policy has not changed, but the shared word has disappeared. An embedding model can represent the relationship between “money back” and “refund”, giving the retriever another way to find the passage.

You will use that approach to build a personal knowledge search engine. It will load your notes, divide them into chunks, create embeddings and store them in a vector database. Searching those vectors lets you look for related ideas even when you cannot remember the original wording.

What you will learn

The project connects the concepts behind semantic search to code you can inspect and test. You will learn to:

  • Explain how an embedding represents text and how similarity search uses it.
  • Store text chunks, vectors and source metadata in a local vector database.
  • Build and search an index of personal notes.
  • Use semantic retrieval in a RAG workflow.
  • Test text-processing helpers separately from live API calls.
  • Describe the project's capabilities and limitations in a portfolio or client demonstration.

Retrieval shapes the answer

A model answering from retrieved context needs passages that actually address the question. If the retriever misses them, a well-written generation prompt cannot supply the missing evidence. Chapter 4 made that dependency visible with keyword matching; this chapter gives you a second retrieval method to compare with it.

A document assistant can follow this sequence:

  1. Load documents and split them into chunks.
  2. Create an embedding for each chunk and store it in a vector database.
  3. Embed the question and retrieve similar chunks.
  4. Give the retrieved context to an LLM to draft an answer.

The same arrangement can support internal knowledge bots, PDF assistants, customer support, research, developer documentation, study notes and business document Q&A. The search engine you build here stops at retrieving and displaying passages, so you can examine their relevance before adding answer generation.

5.1 What Is an Embedding?

An embedding represents text as a vector: a list of numbers produced by a model. For example, this sentence can be converted into a vector:

Customers can request a refund within 30 days.

A shortened, conceptual representation might look like this:

[0.12, -0.04, 0.88, 0.31, ...]

The actual list is usually much longer. You do not need to interpret each number to use it for search; you compare the vector as a whole with other vectors created by the same model. Texts with related meanings may lie close together in that representation.

For instance, these two sentences may produce similar embeddings:

Customers can request a refund.

Customers can get their money back.

That relationship gives a search system a way to connect the sentences despite their different wording.

5.2 What Is Semantic Search?

Semantic search retrieves text by its relationship to a query's meaning. A keyword match remains useful, but it is not the only possible signal. Consider:

Query: How can users reset their password?

Document: Account recovery is available from the login page.

The phrases “reset password” and “account recovery” share no words. An embedding-based search may still retrieve the passage because the ideas are related. Whether it answers the user's particular question is something you must check in the returned text.

5.3 What Is a Vector Database?

A vector database stores embeddings and supports searches for similar vectors. Alongside a vector, this project stores the text it represents and metadata identifying its source. You can think of those as additional fields beyond familiar database fields such as name, email, date, price and status.

When a question arrives, the application creates its embedding, searches the stored vectors and returns the closest chunks. A RAG application can then send those chunks to an LLM. Here you will use Chroma as a local store and display the search results directly.

5.4 Similarity Search

Similarity search compares a query vector with the vectors already stored in the database. Chroma handles the comparison in this project, so you can concentrate on the text being indexed and the results it returns.

For the query "How do I get a refund?", the application creates an embedding, compares it with the stored chunk embeddings and retrieves the closest matches. Those matches are candidates for relevant context. Inspecting them is how you find out whether the retrieval is useful.

5.5 Embeddings vs LLMs

The embedding model and the text-generation model have different jobs in this application. The table separates the output of each from the task it serves:

FeatureEmbedding ModelLLM
Main jobConvert text into vectorsGenerate text
OutputNumbersWords
Used forSearch, clustering, similarityAnswers, summaries, reasoning
ExampleFind relevant document chunksExplain retrieved chunks

In a RAG workflow, embeddings support the search for relevant chunks, while the LLM uses those chunks to write an answer. Keeping the two stages separate also helps you locate errors: a poor answer may begin with a poor retrieval result.

5.6 Why This Improves RAG

Semantic retrieval gives the Chapter 4 assistant a way to handle questions phrased differently from its source. The query and passage below illustrate the problem:

User: Can I get my money back?

Document: Refunds are available within 30 days.

An embedding model may connect the request with the refund policy even without an exact word match. Test that benefit on your own documents: the point of changing the retriever is to find more useful evidence for the answer, not simply to add a vector database.

5.7 Project: Personal Knowledge Search Engine

What the project does

You will build a search engine for local notes with six steps:

  1. Load .txt and .md files from a notes folder.
  2. Split each note into chunks.
  3. Create an embedding for each chunk.
  4. Store the chunks and embeddings in a local Chroma database.
  5. Search the index with a natural-language query.
  6. Display matching chunks with their source information.

Choosing notes to search

Use a small collection you understand: class notes, technical references, freelance project notes, writing research or a personal knowledge base. Knowing the material lets you judge whether the results are useful. You can also use this project to compare retrieval methods before extending a RAG assistant.

Create the following project structure. The loading, chunking, embedding and storage code is kept in separate files so you can inspect each stage:

# Agentic AI With Python Notes

AI agents are software systems that use language models, tools, memory, and workflows to help complete user goals.

RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation. It retrieves relevant information before generating an answer.

Tool calling allows an AI assistant to use approved functions, such as calculators, search tools, or APIs.

Memory helps an assistant remember useful context, but it must be designed carefully to protect privacy.

"""Reusable, lazily connected text-generation client."""
import math
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from openai import OpenAI

load_dotenv()


def get_env_float(name: str, default: float) -> float:
    try:
        value = float(os.getenv(name, str(default)))
        return value if math.isfinite(value) else default
    except ValueError:
        return default


@dataclass
class LLMConfig:
    model: str = field(default_factory=lambda: os.getenv("OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-4.1-mini"))
    temperature: float = field(default_factory=lambda: get_env_float("OPENAI_TEMPERATURE", 0.2))


class LLMClient:
    def __init__(self, config: LLMConfig | None = None, *, client=None):
        self.config = config or LLMConfig()
        self.client = client

    def _get_client(self):
        if self.client is None:
            key = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key == "replace_with_your_api_key":
                raise ValueError("OPENAI_API_KEY is missing. Add a real key to your private .env file for live requests.")
            self.client = OpenAI(api_key=key, timeout=30.0, max_retries=1)
        return self.client

    def complete(self, system: str, user: str) -> str:
        if not isinstance(system, str) or not system.strip():
            raise ValueError("System instruction cannot be empty.")
        if not isinstance(user, str) or not user.strip():
            raise ValueError("User request cannot be empty.")
        client = self._get_client()
        try:
            response = client.responses.create(
                model=self.config.model,
                instructions=system.strip(),
                input=user.strip(),
                temperature=self.config.temperature,
            )
        except Exception as error:
            raise RuntimeError("Model request failed. Check your connection, credentials, quota and model settings.") from error
        text = getattr(response, "output_text", None)
        if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
            raise RuntimeError("Model response did not contain text.")
        return text

"""Load UTF-8 Markdown and text notes in a stable order."""
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS = {".txt", ".md"}


@dataclass
class NoteDocument:
    path: str
    text: str


def is_supported_file(path: Path) -> bool:
    return path.suffix.lower() in SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS


def load_note_file(path: Path) -> NoteDocument:
    path = Path(path)
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {path}")
    if not path.is_file():
        raise ValueError(f"Path is not a file: {path}")
    if not is_supported_file(path):
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported file type: {path.suffix}")
    return NoteDocument(path=str(path), text=path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def load_notes_from_folder(folder: str) -> list[NoteDocument]:
    folder_path = Path(folder)
    if not folder_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Folder not found: {folder}")
    if not folder_path.is_dir():
        raise ValueError(f"Path is not a folder: {folder}")
    return [load_note_file(path) for path in sorted(folder_path.rglob("*"))
            if path.is_file() and is_supported_file(path)]

"""Character-based chunking with source metadata."""
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class TextChunk:
    id: str
    text: str
    source: str
    chunk_index: int


def clean_text(text: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(text.split())


def chunk_text(text: str, chunk_size: int = 800, overlap: int = 120) -> list[str]:
    if type(chunk_size) is not int or chunk_size <= 0:
        raise ValueError("chunk_size must be a positive integer.")
    if type(overlap) is not int or overlap < 0:
        raise ValueError("overlap must be a non-negative integer.")
    if overlap >= chunk_size:
        raise ValueError("overlap must be smaller than chunk_size.")
    cleaned = clean_text(text)
    chunks = []
    start = 0
    while start < len(cleaned):
        end = min(start + chunk_size, len(cleaned))
        chunk = cleaned[start:end].strip()
        if chunk:
            chunks.append(chunk)
        if end == len(cleaned):
            break
        start = end - overlap
    return chunks


def create_chunks_for_document(source: str, text: str, chunk_size: int = 800,
                               overlap: int = 120) -> list[TextChunk]:
    return [TextChunk(f"{source}::chunk_{index}", chunk, source, index)
            for index, chunk in enumerate(chunk_text(text, chunk_size, overlap))]

"""Embedding API boundary; clients can be injected for offline tests."""
import math
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from openai import OpenAI

load_dotenv()


@dataclass
class EmbeddingConfig:
    model: str = field(default_factory=lambda: os.getenv("OPENAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL", "text-embedding-3-small"))


class EmbeddingClient:
    def __init__(self, config: EmbeddingConfig | None = None, *, client=None):
        self.config = config or EmbeddingConfig()
        self.client = client

    def _get_client(self):
        if self.client is None:
            key = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key == "replace_with_your_api_key":
                raise ValueError("OPENAI_API_KEY is missing. Add a real key to your private .env file for live embeddings.")
            self.client = OpenAI(api_key=key, timeout=30.0, max_retries=1)
        return self.client

    def embed_text(self, text: str) -> list[float]:
        return self.embed_texts([text])[0]

    def embed_texts(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        if not texts or any(not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip() for text in texts):
            raise ValueError("Provide at least one text; each text must be non-empty.")
        client = self._get_client()
        try:
            response = client.embeddings.create(model=self.config.model, input=texts)
        except Exception as error:
            raise RuntimeError("Embedding request failed. Check your connection, credentials, quota and embedding model.") from error
        data = list(response.data)
        if len(data) != len(texts) or sorted(item.index for item in data) != list(range(len(texts))):
            raise RuntimeError("Embedding response did not match the input positions.")
        vectors = [list(item.embedding) for item in sorted(data, key=lambda item: item.index)]
        if (not vectors[0] or any(len(vector) != len(vectors[0]) for vector in vectors)
                or any(type(number) not in (int, float) or not math.isfinite(number)
                       for vector in vectors for number in vector)):
            raise RuntimeError("Embedding response contained invalid vectors.")
        return vectors

"""Store and query supplied embeddings with real local Chroma."""
import math
import os

import chromadb
from chromadb.config import Settings
from dotenv import load_dotenv

from embedding_client import EmbeddingClient
from text_utils import TextChunk

load_dotenv()


def get_chroma_path() -> str:
    return os.getenv("CHROMA_PATH", "chroma_db")


def get_collection_name() -> str:
    return os.getenv("COLLECTION_NAME", "personal_notes")


def create_chroma_client():
    return chromadb.PersistentClient(path=get_chroma_path(), settings=Settings(anonymized_telemetry=False))


def get_or_create_collection():
    # Embeddings are always supplied explicitly; do not download a default model.
    return create_chroma_client().get_or_create_collection(
        name=get_collection_name(), embedding_function=None,
    )


def chunk_to_metadata(chunk: TextChunk) -> dict:
    return {"source": chunk.source, "chunk_index": chunk.chunk_index}


def add_chunks_to_vector_store(chunks: list[TextChunk],
                               embedding_client: EmbeddingClient | None = None,
                               *, replace_sources: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Upsert a complete set of chunks for each supplied source, then remove stale IDs.

    Pass replace_sources for an emptied document. Other sources are untouched.
    This local demo is not an atomic multi-writer indexing service.
    """
    if not chunks and not replace_sources:
        return 0
    if len({chunk.id for chunk in chunks}) != len(chunks):
        raise ValueError("Chunk IDs must be unique within an indexing call.")
    if any(not chunk.id or not chunk.source or not chunk.text.strip() for chunk in chunks):
        raise ValueError("Each chunk needs an ID, source and non-empty text.")
    sources = set(replace_sources or []) | {chunk.source for chunk in chunks}
    collection = get_or_create_collection()
    if chunks:
        embedder = embedding_client or EmbeddingClient()
        texts = [chunk.text for chunk in chunks]
        embeddings = embedder.embed_texts(texts)
        if len(embeddings) != len(chunks):
            raise ValueError("Embedding count does not match chunk count.")
        collection.upsert(ids=[chunk.id for chunk in chunks], documents=texts,
                          embeddings=embeddings, metadatas=[chunk_to_metadata(chunk) for chunk in chunks])
    for source in sources:
        current_ids = {chunk.id for chunk in chunks if chunk.source == source}
        old_ids = collection.get(where={"source": source}, include=[])["ids"]
        stale_ids = [identifier for identifier in old_ids if identifier not in current_ids]
        if stale_ids:
            collection.delete(ids=stale_ids)
    return len(chunks)


def search_vector_store(query: str, top_k: int = 5,
                        embedding_client: EmbeddingClient | None = None,
                        *, max_distance: float | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Return nearest candidates; optionally exclude distances above a calibrated limit."""
    if not isinstance(query, str) or not query.strip():
        raise ValueError("Query cannot be empty.")
    if type(top_k) is not int or top_k <= 0:
        raise ValueError("top_k must be a positive integer.")
    if max_distance is not None and (type(max_distance) not in (int, float)
                                    or not math.isfinite(max_distance) or max_distance < 0):
        raise ValueError("max_distance must be a finite non-negative number.")
    collection = get_or_create_collection()
    count = collection.count()
    if count == 0:
        return []
    embedder = embedding_client or EmbeddingClient()
    results = collection.query(query_embeddings=[embedder.embed_text(query)],
                               n_results=min(top_k, count),
                               include=["documents", "metadatas", "distances"])
    output = []
    for identifier, text, metadata, distance in zip(
        results["ids"][0], results["documents"][0], results["metadatas"][0], results["distances"][0]
    ):
        if max_distance is None or distance <= max_distance:
            output.append({"id": identifier, "text": text, "metadata": metadata, "distance": distance})
    return output


def format_search_results(results: list[dict]) -> str:
    if not results:
        return "No results found."
    lines = []
    for index, result in enumerate(results, start=1):
        metadata = result.get("metadata") or {}
        lines.extend([f"Result {index}", f"Source: {metadata.get('source', 'unknown source')}",
                      f"Chunk: {metadata.get('chunk_index', 'unknown')}",
                      f"Distance: {result.get('distance')}", "", result.get("text", ""), "-" * 60])
    return "\n".join(lines)

5.16 File: search_app.py

"""Chapter 5: Personal Knowledge Search Engine."""
from note_loader import load_notes_from_folder
from text_utils import create_chunks_for_document
from vector_store import add_chunks_to_vector_store, search_vector_store, format_search_results


def index_notes(notes_folder: str = "notes", *, embedding_client=None) -> None:
    print(f"\nLoading notes from: {notes_folder}")
    documents = load_notes_from_folder(notes_folder)
    if not documents:
        print("No supported notes found.")
        return
    chunks = [chunk for document in documents
              for chunk in create_chunks_for_document(document.path, document.text)]
    print(f"Created {len(chunks)} chunk(s).")
    print("Creating embeddings and updating vector store...")
    added = add_chunks_to_vector_store(chunks, embedding_client,
                                       replace_sources=[document.path for document in documents])
    print(f"Stored {added} current chunk(s) in vector store.")


def search_loop() -> None:
    print("\nSemantic Search\n" + "=" * 40)
    print("Type a question or search query.\nType /exit to quit.\n" + "=" * 40)
    while True:
        try:
            query = input("\nSearch: ").strip()
        except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
            print("\nGoodbye.")
            break
        if query.lower() in {"/exit", "exit", "quit"}:
            print("Goodbye.")
            break
        if not query:
            print("Please enter a search query.")
            continue
        try:
            results = search_vector_store(query=query, top_k=5)
            print("\nResults:")
            print(format_search_results(results))
        except Exception as error:
            print(f"Search error: {error}")


def main() -> None:
    print("\nPersonal Knowledge Search Engine\n" + "=" * 50)
    print("1. Index notes\n2. Search notes\n" + "=" * 50)
    try:
        choice = input("\nChoose an option: ").strip()
        if choice == "1":
            index_notes()
        elif choice == "2":
            search_loop()
        else:
            print("Unknown option.")
    except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
        print("\nGoodbye.")
    except Exception as error:
        print(f"Indexing error: {error}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import pytest

from note_loader import is_supported_file, load_note_file, load_notes_from_folder


def test_is_supported_file():
    assert is_supported_file(Path("note.md"))
    assert is_supported_file(Path("note.txt"))

def test_load_note_file(tmp_path):

    document = load_note_file(note)
    assert document.path == str(note)
    assert "Hello world" in document.text

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):

    documents = load_notes_from_folder(str(tmp_path))
    assert len(documents) == 2
    assert [Path(document.path).name for document in documents] == ["a.md", "b.txt"]

import pytest

from text_utils import clean_text, chunk_text, create_chunks_for_document


def test_clean_text():
    assert clean_text("Hello  world\nagain") == "Hello world again"


def test_chunk_text_returns_chunks():
    chunks = chunk_text("Python AI agents are useful. " * 100, chunk_size=100, overlap=20)
    assert len(chunks) > 1
    assert all(len(chunk) <= 100 for chunk in chunks)


def test_chunk_text_empty():
    assert chunk_text(" ") == []


def test_chunk_text_invalid_size():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        chunk_text("hello", chunk_size=0)


def test_chunk_text_invalid_overlap():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        chunk_text("hello", chunk_size=100, overlap=100)


def test_create_chunks_for_document():
    chunks = create_chunks_for_document("notes/test.md", "Python AI agents are useful. " * 50, 100, 20)
    assert len(chunks) > 1
    assert chunks[0].source == "notes/test.md"
    assert chunks[0].chunk_index == 0
    assert chunks[0].id == "notes/test.md::chunk_0"


def test_exact_boundary_does_not_add_duplicate_tail():
    assert chunk_text("abcdefghij", 10, 8) == ["abcdefghij"]
    assert chunk_text("abcdefghijkl", 10, 2) == ["abcdefghij", "ijkl"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("size,overlap", [(True, 0), (10.5, 0), (10, True), (10, -1), (10, 1.2)])
def test_chunk_limits_require_integers(size, overlap):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):

5.20 File: README.md

# Personal Knowledge Search Engine

Loads UTF-8 `.md` and `.txt` notes, chunks text, creates embeddings, stores the
vectors in local Chroma, and displays nearest passages with source metadata.

## Setup

Use Python 3.11 or later. Run each chapter from its own project folder.

```sh
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env
```

On Windows PowerShell, activate with `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` and copy with
`Copy-Item .env.example .env`. Add a real API key only for live requests. Imports,

## Tests

```sh
python -m pytest -q
```

Tests inject model/provider responses; they do not call a paid model. This checks
Python control flow, not generated-answer quality, provider availability or pricing.
The reconstructed code was tested with the dependency versions recorded in the
technical repair report. Check provider documentation before a live run.

## Run

Put notes in `notes/`, then run `python search_app.py`. Choose `1` to index or `2`
to search. Live indexing and searches of a populated index send text to the
embedding provider and may incur charges. An empty index returns no results
without contacting the provider.

## Index and retrieval behavior

- Chunk sizes and overlaps are measured in characters after whitespace normalization.
- Indexing upserts each present document and removes obsolete chunks for that source.
  Repeated indexing does not duplicate records. Empty documents clear their old chunks.
- Deleting a source file from disk does not automatically delete its old index records.
  Rebuild the dedicated generated index deliberately to remove deleted sources.
- The indexing call expects all current chunks for each supplied source. It is not an
  atomic transaction or a concurrent-writer indexing service.
- Keep the same embedding model and dimensionality within a collection. Use a new
  collection or rebuild if the model changes; same-size incompatible vectors are
  not automatically detected by this teaching implementation.
- `top_k` is a positive integer and is capped to the collection size. Closest passages
  are candidates, not verified answers. Optional `max_distance` filters weak matches;
  calibrate it on your own model/data rather than copying a universal threshold.
- The integration tests use real persistent Chroma and an explicitly deterministic,
  hand-written embedding fixture. They prove storage/routing behavior, not semantic
  model quality. No model download is required by the tests.
- Local Chroma data are generated files in `chroma_db/`. Do not send secrets or
  unapproved private notes to the embedding service.

5.21 How the Code Works

Follow a note through these five stages to see where its text and source information go.

Stage 1: Load Notes

The loader reads Markdown and text files from notes/:

documents = load_notes_from_folder("notes")

Each document carries its path and text. The path will also identify the source of any matching chunks.

Stage 2: Chunk Notes

The chunking function divides each document into smaller text records:

chunks = create_chunks_for_document(
    source=document.path,
    text=document.text,
)

Each record contains id, text, source and chunk_index. Retaining the source and position lets a reader trace a search result back to its note.

Stage 3: Create Embeddings

The embedding client sends the chunk texts to the embedding API and receives their numeric vectors:

embeddings = embedder.embed_texts(texts)

This is the part of indexing that needs network access and can incur API charges.

Stage 4: Store in Chroma

Chroma stores the chunk id, chunk text, embedding and metadata together. A result can therefore include both the matched text and the information needed to locate its source.

Stage 5: Search by Meaning

The search function embeds the query and compares it with the stored chunk vectors:

results = search_vector_store(query="How do agents use tools?")

The command-line interface displays the closest chunks for you to inspect. An empty index returns no results without an embedding call. For a populated index, nearest does not necessarily mean relevant: the optional max_distance argument can filter candidates after you calibrate a limit on your own model and documents.

5.25 Debugging Semantic Search

When a search returns an unexpected result, check the indexed notes, their chunks and the query before changing the answer-generation prompt. This table gives you starting points:

ProblemLikely CauseFix
No resultsNotes not indexedRun indexing first
Old resultsDatabase contains old chunksDelete chroma_db/ and reindex
Bad resultsPoor chunksAdjust chunk size
API errorMissing keyCheck .env
Unexpected old recordsA source was deleted or renamed on diskRebuild the dedicated index deliberately; ordinary reindexing replaces present sources only
Slow indexingLarge notesIndex fewer files first
Poor relevanceQuery too vagueAsk more specific question

For this local demo, you can rebuild a stale index by removing its generated database directory and indexing the notes again. Check that you are in the project folder and that chroma_db contains only the index you intend to discard.

On macOS or Linux:

rm -rf chroma_db

On Windows PowerShell:

Remove-Item -Recurse -Force chroma_db

Run indexing again after the reset.

5.26 Embeddings and Metadata

The vector helps retrieve a chunk; its metadata tells you where that chunk came from. A relevant-looking passage is much easier to inspect when the result includes a source reference.

Depending on the collection, useful metadata may include:

source file
page number
chunk index
document title
created date
document type

This project stores source and chunk_index. Those fields give the local notes demo a basic reference back to each file. Add further fields when a reader needs, for example, a document title or page number to verify a result.

5.30 Common Mistakes

Mistake 1: Confusing Embeddings with Chat Responses

An embedding call returns numbers for comparison. A text-generation call returns a written response. Keep those responsibilities separate when tracing a retrieval or answer problem.

Mistake 2: Forgetting to Store Metadata

Store source information with each chunk so readers can locate the passage and check it in context.

Mistake 3: Reindexing Without Checking Existing Records

Indexing now replaces the chunks belonging to each present source and removes that source's obsolete chunk IDs. Empty notes clear their earlier chunks. Files deleted or renamed on disk are not automatically removed from the collection, so rebuild the dedicated generated index when you need a complete reset. Do not run concurrent indexing writers against this teaching implementation.

Mistake 4: Testing Only One Query

Try several phrasings of the same question. This tests the reason for using semantic search: finding related content when the wording changes.

Mistake 5: Ignoring Chunk Quality

Read the chunks themselves when relevance is poor. A passage cut away from its explanation may be difficult to retrieve or interpret usefully.

Mistake 6: Sending Secrets in Notes

Do not index API keys, passwords, private tokens or confidential material without the required permission and security arrangements. In this project, creating embeddings sends note text to an external API even though the database is local.

Mistake 7: Treating Distance Scores as Universal

Distance scores depend on the system and configuration. Use them to compare results within the relevant setup, and inspect the text before deciding whether a match is good enough.

5.31 Keeping the Index Useful

Build the index from readable chunks, retain their source metadata and choose a collection name that identifies the material. Keep the generated database out of Git, and rebuild it deliberately when you change the chunking strategy.

Test several query styles and inspect the passages before feeding them to an LLM. Record the limitations in README, including weak queries and any restrictions on the source material. Review notes for secrets before sending their text to the embedding service.

5.33 Chapter Summary

The project brings loading, chunking, embedding and storage together in a searchable collection of notes. Chroma returns matching chunks, and their source metadata lets you inspect where they came from. That retrieval stage can replace the keyword retriever in the Chapter 4 PDF assistant once you have compared the results.

Chapter 6 introduces tools: Python functions that an assistant can select and run under application control. Your search function will be one candidate for that kind of tool.

Key takeaways

  • Embeddings represent text as numeric vectors that can be compared for similarity.
  • Related meaning can help retrieve a passage even when the query uses different words.
  • A vector database stores those representations and supports similarity searches.
  • Source metadata makes retrieved passages traceable.
  • Retrieval and answer generation have separate jobs and need separate inspection.
  • A portfolio demonstration should show the search behaviour you have actually tested.
